newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC chief revises universal phone plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC chief revises universal phone plan.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission proposed Tuesday to slash the multi-billion-dollar federal fund to be used to subsidize high-cost phone service by relying only on proceeds derived from interstate phone revenues.

FCC Chairman Reed Hundt conceded before a meeting of state regulators his suggestion would not follow the advice of a joint federal state board that last year proposed mingling funds derived from interstate and intrastate phone traffic to subsidize high-cost phone service.

Hundt said his latest proposal reflects the realization that the existing plan lacks adequate support from state regulators around the country. State officials would prefer to have control over intrastate revenues to subsidize so-called universal phone service.
"I do not want to be in another civil war over jurisdiction," Hundt told a meeting of the National Association of Regulatory and Utility Commissioners.
Hundt said his proposal would mean a smaller federal pot for subsidizing high-cost phone service.

Last year, Hundt had said a joint fund to subsidize universal service would require anywhere from $10 billion to $20 billion. He said the current fund he envisions that relies only on money derived from interstate service would "clearly be single-digit."
Historically the FCC share in subsidizing universal service had amounted to about 25 percent while the states' proportion totaled the remaining 75 percent.
"We'll do our part. And they'll have to do their part," Hundt told reporters, referring to the states.
